dedupe_keys.name: foodrest french household fruit and vegetable waste behaviour and spoilage data

description: FOODREST combines measured fruit and vegetable waste with household practices and spoilage observations. Université de Bretagne Occidentale researchers publish connected-bin measurements from forty-nine volunteer households, interviews, refrigerator descriptors, microbial results, controlled spoilage assays and two wider French consumer surveys. The article reports 1,048 and 815 respondents in those surveys. Repository coverage is 2021–2024, with household fieldwork around Brest and broader national survey recruitment. Recherche Data Gouv lists twenty-two unrestricted tables and documents under the Etalab Open Licence 2.0, allowing free access. Volunteer selection, differing samples and laboratory storage conditions are limitations when inferring national waste volumes. Modellers could parameterise household waste-generation decisions or spoilage processes in food-system simulations. data-fao-food-loss-and-waste-database and data-tulcan-household-food-waste-survey provide related resources. The listed interview transcripts are described as anonymised; none were downloaded or read. The review also did not inspect household rows, microbial sequences or measured bin data.
